d.chapter: Economic Geography — Natural Regions: 3. Desert Regions
d.notions: Oasis, water table, irrigation, shaduf, foggara, borehole, date palm.
d.focus: Formation of oases and farming around oases; irrigation in hot deserts.
d.competence: Learners are able to explain how water can be brought to crops in the dry season and use water carefully in farming.
objectives: Explain how an oasis is formed.
Describe the crops grown in oases.
Describe the methods of irrigation used in deserts.
Identify the problems of oasis farming.
recall: Desert people face lack of water, extreme temperatures, sandstorms and poor soils.
They adapt through nomadism, camels, clothing, housing and wells.
d.recallNote: Check the homework: the name of an oasis and its country.
situation: In the middle of the Sahara, travellers see a green area with tall palm trees, gardens and houses, while all around there is only sand and rock.
Musa, who is travelling with them, wonders how crops can grow in this place where it almost never rains.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Musa does not understand how crops can grow in a desert place where it almost never rains.
What did the travellers see in the green area?
They saw tall palm trees, gardens and houses.
Where do you think the water for these crops comes from?
The water probably comes from under the ground, from a well or a spring.
d.justification: This lesson will help us to understand how people farm in the desert thanks to oases and irrigation.

qa.q: Look at the diagram. Where does the water of an oasis come from?
qa.a: The water comes from rain that fell on distant highlands. It flows slowly under the desert in permeable rock and comes to the surface in a low place.

qa.q: What do we call a fertile place in the desert where underground water reaches the surface?
qa.a: Such a fertile place is called an oasis. Examples are Siwa in Egypt and Tafilalt in Morocco.

sum.title: I. The Oasis
defs: An oasis is a fertile place in the desert where underground water reaches the surface or can be reached by wells.
items: Rain falls on distant highlands, flows slowly under the desert in permeable rock and reaches the surface in low places.
Famous oases include Siwa in Egypt and Tafilalt in Morocco. The Nile valley is like a long oasis in the desert.

qa.q: Look at the diagram. Name the three layers of crops grown in an oasis.
qa.a: The top layer is made of date palms, the middle layer of fruit trees such as citrus, figs and pomegranates, and the ground layer of vegetables, wheat and barley.

qa.q: Why do farmers grow crops in three layers under the date palms?
qa.a: The tall palms give shade and protect the smaller plants from the strong sun and the wind. This also uses the little land well.

qa.q: Farmers in Egypt used a long pole with a bucket to lift water from the Nile. What is this tool called?
qa.a: This tool is called a shaduf. Today, farmers mostly use motor pumps and boreholes.

qa.q: Farmers use too much water from their wells. What happens to the water table and to the soil?
qa.a: The water table falls, so wells dry up. The soil also becomes salty because of evaporation.

sum.title: II. Farming around Oases
sum.intro: Farming around oases has the following characteristics:
items: Date palms form the top layer, fruit trees the middle layer, and vegetables, wheat and barley the ground layer.
Water is brought from wells, springs and underground channels (foggaras), with the shaduf or with motor pumps and boreholes.
In Egypt, the Aswan High Dam on the Nile stores water in Lake Nasser to irrigate fields all year.
Wells dry up when too much water is used, soils become salty, and sand dunes invade the fields.

evaluation: Explain how an oasis is formed.
Rain falls on distant highlands and flows slowly under the desert. It reaches the surface in a low place, forming an oasis.
Why is the date palm important in an oasis?
It gives dates to eat and sell, and it shades and protects the smaller crops below it.
Give two problems of oasis farming.
Wells can dry up and soils can become salty.
remediation: A fertile place in the desert with water is called an ______.
The main tree of oases is the ______ palm.
A pole with a bucket used to lift water is a ______.
The dam on the Nile in Egypt is the Aswan ______ Dam.
The level of underground water is called the water ______.
d.remediationAnswers: 1. oasis 2. date 3. shaduf 4. foggaras 5. High 6. table
